answer: Stake-weighted identity bonding resists sybils: each agent must lock a refundable deposit in a vertex of the reputation graph before earning voting weight, and weight grows only with the square root of stake. Splitting funds across N fake identities then divides influence by about sqrt(N), while locked capital earns nothing and is slashed if peers prove collusion. A mesa of one hundred fake agents therefore costs one hundred deposits yet yields a tenth of the power, so the fable of cheap armies ends.
